# Noreja Intelligence GmbH

> Noreja is a Generative Process Intelligence platform for analyzing and improving business processes by combining operational data, causal process models, contextual knowledge, and generative AI.

Noreja Intelligence GmbH (Hohenweiler, Austria) provides a B2B SaaS platform that connects directly to relational data sources and models process events, business objects, and their relationships in an Event Knowledge Graph, without requiring users to prepare a traditional flat event log. Every case is compared with an expected order defined with domain knowledge (causal process mining), and the results are combined with company context and generative AI. In 2026 Gartner recognized Noreja in "Coolest Vendor Innovations in Process Intelligence".

The product areas are:

- Dashboard: Configurable monitoring of process metrics, trends, distributions, variants, and anomalies per perspective.
- Analyzer: Interactive exploration of processes in the Process, Case, Pattern, and Timeline views, including bottlenecks, violations of the expected order, rework, and performance metrics.
- Builder: Data-source connectivity, entity modeling, and perspectives (formerly called dimensions) with their case ID and expected order, plus import management.
- Workbench: A personal JupyterLab environment for custom analysis on the Noreja Knowledge Graph.
- Minerva and the AI Hub: Minerva 2.0 is the AI assistant that reads the causal process graph and company knowledge from the Context Hub, plans multi-step tasks, uses skills and sub-agents, and creates files; it is configured in the AI Hub and runs with local or cloud models chosen per chat.

The Platform page presents these as a closed loop of four phases (Insights, Action, Impact, Feedback) with one agent type per phase.

Interpretation guidance:

- Use the Platform page for the current product scope and capabilities.
- Use the Help Center for current technical behavior, configuration guidance, integrations, and release information. Its own index is at https://docs.noreja.com/en/llms.txt, and every article is available as Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL.
- Current product terminology: perspective (formerly dimension), expected order (formerly causal hypothesis or causal model), and the process patterns Disarray, Negligence, and Rework (violations) and Simplification and Reorder (allowed deviations).
- "Agent" has four related senses at Noreja: Minerva agents and sub-agents in the product, the ten specialized agents of the Minerva Agent Library, the Minerva Frontier Agents, and the four loop agent types on the Platform page. See section 10 of https://noreja.com/llms-full.txt.
- Use the Pricing page for current plans and commercial details; do not rely on prices copied into cached summaries.
- Use the Trust Center and legal pages for current security, privacy, compliance, and contractual information.
- Treat quantified performance, savings, and customer outcomes as context-specific unless the linked source states otherwise. Figures on the end-to-end process pages come from synthetic demonstration datasets.
- Treat the Competitive Comparisons below as Noreja's own positioning rather than an independent evaluation; for any current factual claim about another vendor, prefer that vendor's own documentation.
- English is the primary language of this file. The website and Help Center are also available in German; German page URLs are listed at the end.

## Product and Documentation

- [Platform Overview](https://noreja.com/en/platform): Current overview of Noreja's improvement loop (Insights, Action, Impact, Feedback), its four agent types, the causal process model, and the product areas.
- [Minerva 2.0](https://noreja.com/en/minerva): The AI assistant for process intelligence: plain-language questions about processes, answers grounded in the causal process graph and the Context Hub, skills and sub-agents, files such as Excel, Word, PDF, and PowerPoint, and local or cloud models.
- [Minerva Agent Library](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents): Ten specialized AI agents for business process analysis, grouped into process flow and conformance, time and deadlines, capital and work in progress, and root causes and potential.
- [Minerva Frontier Agents](https://noreja.com/en/frontier-agents): Context-aware AI agents that work continuously in the background on a specific question, monitoring processes, maintaining process models, and flagging deviations, data-source changes, and compliance risks.
- [Product Documentation and Help Center](https://docs.noreja.com/en): Technical documentation, configuration guides, integrations, feature explanations, and release notes.
- [Help Center Index for LLMs](https://docs.noreja.com/en/llms.txt): Machine-readable index of all English Help Center articles with links to their Markdown versions.
- [Pricing](https://noreja.com/en/pricing): Current plans, included modules, user allowances, services, pricing parameters, and commercial FAQs.
- [FAQ](https://noreja.com/en/faq): Answers on technology and methodology, implementation and Proof-of-Value, licensing and pricing, data hosting and security, and analyst recognition.
- [Full Website](https://noreja.com/en): Main English-language website and high-level introduction to Noreja Generative Process Intelligence.

## Minerva Agent Library

- [Structural Deviation Analysis Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/structural-deviation-analysis-agent): Finds skipped steps, swapped sequences, and paths that should not exist according to the target process, and shows what they cost.
- [Rework Analysis Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/rework-analysis-agent): Calculates the rework rate, finds loops and repeated steps, and connects them with their causes.
- [Compliance Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/compliance-agent): Checks every case against policies such as approval limits, four-eyes principle, and segregation of duties, and backs up each finding.
- [Cycle Time Analysis Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/cycle-time-analysis-agent): Measures cycle times per case, transition, and variant, shows the distribution rather than just the average, and explains the outliers.
- [Waiting Time Analysis Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/waiting-time-analysis-agent): Finds idle time between steps, bottlenecks, and the reasons why work sits still.
- [On-Time Performance Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/on-time-performance-agent): Measures on-time delivery, OTIF, and SLA compliance and shows at which step commitments are missed.
- [Working Capital Analysis Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/working-capital-analysis-agent): Shows where capital is tied up in purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash: early payments, lost cash discounts, and late incoming payments.
- [WIP Analysis Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/wip-analysis-agent): Counts open cases per process step, shows their age, and detects where a backlog is building up.
- [Root Cause Analysis Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/root-cause-analysis-agent): Traces dependencies in the causal process graph and explains process problems with evidence.
- [Automation Potential Agent](https://noreja.com/en/minerva/agents/automation-potential-agent): Finds manual, uniform steps, measures the automation rate, and ranks candidates by potential.

## Knowledge and Concepts

- [Definitions and Glossary](https://noreja.com/en/definitions): Index of Noreja's English-language explanations of Process Intelligence, Process Mining, causal modeling, event data, process-modeling notations (BPMN, EPC), and agentic AI concepts. All definition pages are listed in the next section.
- [Welcome to Noreja](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/welcome-to-noreja): What Noreja does, the idea of causal process mining behind it, what Minerva can do, and a first orientation in the product areas.
- [Help Center Glossary](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/glossary): Noreja product terms with one-sentence explanations, including earlier names such as dimension and causal model.
- [The Origin of Causal Process Mining](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/the-origin-of-causal-process-mining): Why classical process mining produces spaghetti models when business objects are connected 1:N or N:M, and how Causal Process Mining uses relational structure and expert knowledge about cause and effect instead.
- [The Expected Order](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/the-expected-order-perspective-hypothesis-shortcuts-and-backjumps): How the expected order (perspective hypothesis) of a perspective works, and what allowed shortcuts and backjumps mean.
- [Process Patterns](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/process-patterns-disarray-negligence-rework-and-allowed-deviations): The five process patterns Noreja recognises when cases deviate from the expected order: Disarray, Negligence, Rework, Simplification, and Reorder.
- [What Minerva Can Do](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/what-minerva-can-do): How Minerva works with agents, skills, and sub-agents, which data it uses, what it creates, what it can't do, and what happens with the data.
- [Noreja's Agents and Skills](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/noreja-s-agents-and-skills): The agents and skills Noreja ships for Minerva: Minerva and Minerva (On-Premise), the background sub-agents, and the skills users can start with "/".
- [Context Hub: Knowledge for Minerva](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/context-hub-knowledge-for-minerva): How company knowledge, documents, and notes are added for Minerva, who may use them, and with which AI models.
- [Minerva: Models, Data Flow and Data Protection](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/minerva-models-data-flow-and-data-protection): Which AI models Minerva uses, which data goes to them, what always stays with the local model, and how long chats and files are kept.
- [Prepare Your Source Data](https://docs.noreja.com/en/article/prepare-your-source-data-keys-timestamps-indices): What the tables of a data source should offer for a good process model: stable keys, linking columns, clean timestamps, and indexes for fast imports.
- [Cost of Inaction Calculator](https://noreja.com/en/cost-of-inaction): Interactive estimate of the hidden annual cost of unimproved end-to-end processes, split across the four process dimensions time, cost, quality, and complexity; includes an interactive Devil's Quadrangle showing why time trades off against cost and quality against flexibility.
- [Smart Data Forge](https://noreja.com/en/smart-data-forge): Free browser-based generator for synthetic, causally consistent process data with a deliberately built-in root cause; defines tables, causal chains, deviations, and value distributions and exports DDL and INSERT scripts for PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, and Oracle. Access requires an email address.

## Definitions

- [Process Mining](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-mining): Definition, purpose, and business relevance of Process Mining.
- [Process Intelligence](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-intelligence): Definition of Process Intelligence and its relationship to Process Mining, contextual knowledge, and AI.
- [Process Intelligence versus Process Mining](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-intelligence-vs-process-mining): Explanation of the difference between the analysis method and the wider discipline built on it.
- [Graph Databases](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/graph-databases): Explanation of graph-based data storage and its relevance to connected process data.
- [Event Knowledge Graph](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/event-knowledge-graph): Explanation of event and business-object representation in a connected graph structure.
- [Causal Process Mining](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/causal-process-mining): Definition of causal process analysis based on relationships beyond temporal sequence.
- [Limitations of Directly-Follows Approaches](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/directly-follows-limitations): Explanation of representational limitations in directly-follows process models.
- [Event Log](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/event-log): Definition of the traditional event-log format used in Process Mining.
- [Business Process Management](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/business-process-management): Definition of BPM and its relationship to process analysis and improvement.
- [Process](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/what-is-a-process): Definition of a business process, its boundaries, inputs, activities, and outputs.
- [Object-Centric Process Mining](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/object-centric-process-mining): Explanation of process analysis involving multiple related business-object types.
- [Process Discovery](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-discovery): Explanation of automatically deriving process models from observed event data.
- [Conformance Checking](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/conformance-checking): Explanation of comparing observed process behavior with policies or target models.
- [Task Mining](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/task-mining): Explanation of analyzing user interactions and manual desktop-level work.
- [OCEL 2.0](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/ocel-2): Explanation of the Object-Centric Event Log 2.0 standard.
- [Process Variant](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-variant): Definition of a distinct execution path through a process.
- [Process Instance](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-instance): Definition of a single execution or case of a process.
- [Process Simulation](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-simulation): Explanation of evaluating potential process changes through simulation.
- [Digital Process Twin](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/digital-process-twin): Explanation of a data-driven digital representation of an operational process.
- [To-Be and As-Is Processes](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/to-be-vs-as-is-process): Explanation of current-state and target-state process models.
- [BPMN](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/bpmn): Explanation of the Business Process Model and Notation standard for graphical process modeling.
- [Event-driven Process Chain (EPC)](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/epk): Explanation of the EPC notation of alternating events and functions, widely used in German-speaking countries.
- [Agentic AI](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-ai): Definition of AI systems that pursue a goal independently across multiple steps by planning, using tools, and acting.
- [AI Agent](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/ai-agent): Definition of an AI agent, its building blocks, and how it differs from a chatbot or RPA bot.
- [Agentic AI versus Generative AI](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-ai-vs-generative-ai): Explanation of the difference between producing content and carrying out tasks, and what it means for control.
- [Frontier Agents](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/frontier-agents): Explanation of autonomous, long-running AI agents that stay on a goal persistently instead of answering on demand.
- [Agentic Process Intelligence](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-process-intelligence): Explanation of autonomous AI agents working continuously on process models and process data.
- [Agent Mining](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agent-mining): Explanation of applying Process Mining methods to the event traces produced by AI agents.
- [Agent Conformance Checking](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agent-conformance-checking): Explanation of verifying that an autonomous agent stayed within its permitted process, role, and policy boundaries.
- [Process Grounding](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-grounding): Explanation of anchoring language-model output in real process and event data rather than linguistic probability.
- [Causal AI](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/causal-ai): Explanation of AI that models cause-and-effect relationships rather than statistical association alone.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/model-context-protocol): Explanation of the open standard through which AI models and agents access external data sources and tools.
- [Agentic Automation versus RPA](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-automation-vs-rpa): Explanation of the difference between prescribed rule execution and goal-driven decisions at runtime.
- [AI Agent versus Copilot](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/ai-agent-vs-copilot): Explanation of the difference in initiative, time horizon, and scope of action between agents and copilots.
- [Self-Improving Processes](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/self-improving-processes): Explanation of processes that run their own continuous measure-understand-intervene loop.
- [Process Ontology](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/process-ontology): Explanation of the semantic layer describing object types, events, and their relationships in a process domain.
- [Agentic Root Cause Analysis](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-root-cause-analysis): Explanation of agents forming and testing root-cause hypotheses against process data.
- [Agent Readiness of Process Data](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agent-readiness): Explanation of the data conditions required for AI agents to work reliably on process data.
- [Agentic Process Automation (APA)](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-process-automation): Explanation of automating processes with goal-driven AI agents that handle the exceptions rule-based automation cannot.
- [Agentic Process Mining](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-process-mining): Explanation of process mining carried out by AI agents that drive the analysis themselves.
- [Context Engineering](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/context-engineering): Explanation of designing the information, tools, and rules an AI agent receives at the moment of a decision.
- [Human-in-the-Loop](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/human-in-the-loop): Explanation of defined points where a person reviews or approves before an AI agent acts.
- [Agent Orchestration](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agent-orchestration): Explanation of coordinating multiple AI agents, rule-based automation, and people within one end-to-end process.
- [Multi-Agent System](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/multi-agent-system): Explanation of several specialized AI agents solving one task together.
- [Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/a2a-protocol): Explanation of the open standard through which AI agents from different platforms exchange tasks.
- [AI Agent Governance](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/ai-agent-governance): Explanation of the rules, roles, and controls that determine what AI agents are allowed to do.
- [Guardian Agents](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/guardian-agents): Explanation of AI agents that supervise other AI agents and can intervene during execution.
- [Agent Observability (AgentOps)](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agent-observability): Explanation of tracing and operating AI agents to see what they do, cost, and get wrong.
- [Agentic BPM](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agentic-bpm): Explanation of business process management for processes in which AI agents make decisions within a process frame.
- [Agent Washing](https://noreja.com/en/definitions/agent-washing): Explanation of marketing chatbots, assistants, or RPA as agentic without real agentic capabilities.

## Competitive Comparisons

- [Process Intelligence Vendor Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards): Factual overview comparing leading process mining and process intelligence platforms; explains the distinction between frequency-based Directly-Follows analysis and Noreja's causal, temporal approach on an Event Knowledge Graph.
- [Noreja vs. Celonis Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/celonis): Head-to-head comparison of analysis paradigm, data model, ecosystem lock-in, and pricing transparency.
- [Noreja vs. Signavio Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/sap-signavio): Comparison with SAP Signavio, focused on SAP-ecosystem dependence versus source-system-agnostic causal analysis.
- [Noreja vs. UiPath Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/uipath-process-mining): Comparison with UiPath Process Mining, focused on automation-first discovery versus causal diagnosis.
- [Noreja vs. IBM Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/ibm-process-mining): Comparison with IBM Process Mining, focused on object-centric frequency mining (OCPM) versus causal modeling.
- [Noreja vs. Microsoft Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/microsoft-process-mining): Comparison with Microsoft Process Mining, focused on Power Platform accessibility versus analytical depth.
- [Noreja vs. ServiceNow Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/servicenow-process-mining): Comparison with ServiceNow Process Mining, focused on platform-native ITSM scope versus cross-system end-to-end analysis.
- [Noreja vs. ABBYY Timeline Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/abbyy-timeline): Comparison with ABBYY Timeline, focused on document-centric mining versus a graph-based causal model.
- [Noreja vs. Appian Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/appian): Comparison with Appian, focused on low-code orchestration with add-on mining versus specialized causal diagnosis.
- [Noreja vs. ARIS Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/aris-process-mining): Comparison with ARIS Process Mining, focused on model-repository conformance versus data-driven causal analysis.
- [Noreja vs. MPMX Comparison](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/mpmx-mehrwerk): Comparison with mpmX (MEHRWERK), focused on Qlik-based frequency analysis versus a dedicated causal graph model.
- [Top 10 Process Mining Tools 2027](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/top-10/process-mining-tools): Ranked overview of ten process mining tools (Noreja, Celonis, SAP Signavio, ARIS, UiPath, Microsoft, IBM, QPR, Apromore, Disco) by data model, analysis depth, time to insight, openness and pricing transparency. Published by Noreja, which ranks itself first by disclosed criteria.
- [Top 10 Process Intelligence Platforms 2027](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/top-10/process-intelligence-platforms): Ranked overview of ten process intelligence platforms after Gartner renamed its process mining Magic Quadrant to "Process Intelligence Platforms" in May 2026; criteria are context model, AI and agent readiness, path to action and openness. Published by Noreja.
- [Top 10 Celonis Alternatives 2027](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/top-10/celonis-alternatives): Ten alternatives to Celonis, each with what it does differently and when Celonis remains the better fit. Published by Noreja.
- [Top 10 Process Intelligence Agents 2027](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/top-10/process-intelligence-agents): Ten types of AI agents for process analysis (root cause, structural deviation, compliance, automation potential, cycle time, waiting time, rework, working capital, on-time performance, work in progress), each mapped to an agent of the Minerva Agent Library.
- [Top 10 AI Process Mining Tools 2027](https://noreja.com/en/battle-cards/top-10/ai-process-mining-tools): Ten process mining tools ranked by what their AI does – copilots, agents, MCP interfaces, AI root-cause analysis – and how well the data model grounds it. Published by Noreja.

## End-to-End Processes

- [End-to-End Processes Overview](https://noreja.com/en/processes): Index of end-to-end processes analyzed with causal process mining, with phases, findings, causes, and measures for each.
- [Lead-to-Activation](https://noreja.com/en/processes/lead-to-activation): The end-to-end process from a new lead to an active service, shown for a district heating connection: process phases (sales, parallel trade coordination, construction and commissioning, handover and start of supply), the business objects involved, and four findings on offer rework, seasonal construction times, handover compliance and construction-start prerequisites. Figures come from a synthetic demonstration dataset. Full case (German): https://docs.noreja.com/de/article/lead-to-activation-fernwarmeanschluss
- [Premium-to-Tax](https://noreja.com/en/processes/premium-to-tax): The end-to-end process from a tax-relevant insurance premium transaction to the paid insurance premium tax (IPT): eleven core activities in four phases (capture and tax determination, GL posting and reconciliation, tax return and approval, filing and payment), the source and context objects involved, and six deviations – skipped risk-location determination, filing before approval, calculation rework after reconciliation, approval rework, cases ending after reconciliation and filed but unpaid returns. Figures come from a synthetic demonstration dataset. Full case (German): https://docs.noreja.com/de/article/premium-to-tax-p2t
- [Purchase-to-Pay](https://noreja.com/en/processes/purchase-to-pay): The end-to-end process from an internal procurement need to payment, shown for procurement in special machine building: four phases (requirement and approval, purchase order and fulfilment path for physical goods and software, goods receipt and batched inspection, invoice, approval and payment), the business objects involved, five findings on maverick buying, invoice rework explained with ticket context, shared inspection capacity, payments outside the cash discount period and supplier performance, a Minerva cause model and example fields of action. Figures come from a synthetic demonstration dataset. Full case (German): https://docs.noreja.com/de/article/purchase-to-pay-einkauf-im-sondermaschinenbau
- [Order-to-Cash](https://noreja.com/en/processes/order-to-cash): The end-to-end process from order entry to payment clearing, shown for touchless processing of configured customer orders: three phases (order entry, configuration and release; delivery and invoicing; payment, dunning and complaint), the business objects involved, and five findings on the touchless rate as a KPI that shows the what but not the why, complaints concentrated on technical and service configurations, skipped order reviews classified as an error pattern rather than a new variant, a root cause analysis with Minerva in which special values rather than order changes separate the complaint risk, and a resulting risk-based review rule; plus why AI needs causal process mining and how findings are prioritised in the Business Impact Board. Figures come from a synthetic demonstration dataset. Full case (German): https://docs.noreja.com/de/article/order-to-cash-touchless-aber-nicht-um-jeden-preis

## Videos

- [Four Experts, Five Opinions](https://noreja.com/en/four-experts-five-opinions): Five-part talk series (in German) with Thomas Heinrichs and Dominik Horn from partner Miragon and Jan Mendling and Lukas Pfahlsberger from Noreja: organisational hurdles of process intelligence, why process mining often creates no impact, process discovery beyond the quick event log, IT governance as the real blocker of AI initiatives, and why products will integrate into AI rather than the other way round.
